learning_outcomes.text: Understanding and mastery of basic concepts about the general laws of mechanics, thermodynamics, fields and waves, and electromagnetism, and their application to solving engineering problems.
Knowledge in basic and technological subjects, enabling them to learn new methods and theories, and providing them with versatility to adapt to new situations.
Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity, critical reasoning, and to communicate and transmit knowledge, skills, and abilities in the field of industrial engineering.
Knows the units, orders of magnitude of defined physical quantities, and solves basic engineering problems, expressing the numerical result in appropriate physical units.
Correctly uses basic methods of experimental measurement or simulation, and processes, presents, and interprets the obtained data, relating them to appropriate physical quantities and laws.
Knows the fundamental concepts and laws of mechanics and thermodynamics and their application to basic problems in Engineering.
Understands the meaning, usefulness, and relationships between fundamental elastic quantities, moduli, and coefficients used in solids and fluids.
Correctly performs mass and energy balances in fluid movements in the presence of basic devices.
Correctly uses the concepts of temperature and heat. Applies them to calorimetric, thermal expansion, and heat transfer problems.
Applies the first and second principles of thermodynamics to processes, basic cycles, and thermal machines.
Uses bibliography, by any currently available means, and uses clear and precise language in explanations on physics issues.
Correctly applies the fundamental equations of mechanics to various fields of physics and engineering: rigid body dynamics, oscillations, elasticity, fluids, electromagnetism, and waves.
Analyzes problems that integrate different aspects of Physics I, recognizing the varied physical foundations underlying a technical application, device, or real system.

assessment_methods.method: Written test on topics 7 to 10 (end of semester)

assessment_rules: The course can be evaluated through continuous assessment or a global assessment. For continuous assessment, a mid-semester written test on topics 1-6 accounts for 40% of the grade, provided a minimum of 4.5 out of 10 is achieved. A final written test on topics 7-10 accounts for another 40%, and a written exam on laboratory practices accounts for 20%, given attendance to practice sessions. If continuous assessment is not followed, a global assessment consists of an exam on topics 1-10 for 80% and a laboratory practices exam for 20% (or an additional practical exam for non-attendees). Academic fraud results in a 0 for the test and may lead to disciplinary action.
